ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Hong Kong: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615); Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) Part 12 and Schedule 5B on Register of Significant Controllers; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310); Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 38); Limited Partnership Fund Ordinance (Cap. 637); HKMA AML/CFT Guidelines (current version); and, for PRC-connected beneficial owners, PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 (Measures for the Identification and Filing of Beneficial Owners, effective 1 November 2024).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Foreign-Invested Partnership Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certify the certificate as a true copy before a Hong Kong notary public; if the destination state is an Apostille Convention member, obtain an Apostille from the High Court of Hong Kong; if the destination state is not an Apostille Convention member, submit the notarized certificate to the destination state's embassy or consulate in Hong Kong or Beijing for consular legalization. The apostille and consular legalization routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; they must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Continuing Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain the Registrar's certificate, have it attested by a Hong Kong notary public, then either obtain an Apostille from the High Court of Hong Kong for a Hague member destination or obtain consular legalization from the destination state's consulate for a non-member destination; choose only one route.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney appointing incorporation agent and legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General partners of CN_FIP and Hong Kong notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute the resolution and power of attorney before all general partners, have signatures notarized by a Hong Kong notary public, then apply to the High Court of Hong Kong for an Apostille if the destination is an Apostille Convention state; otherwise have the notarized instrument legalized by the destination state's consulate. Do not combine apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign-Invested Partnership CN_FIP and Hong Kong Companies Registry (where filed)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certify the constitutive instrument by a Hong Kong notary public, then route through either the Hong Kong High Court Apostille for Apostille Convention states or consular legalization at the destination state's diplomatic mission for non-member states; these are alternative authentication mechanisms.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong licensed bank maintained by the investors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain the original on bank letterhead signed by an authorized signatory, have the signature certified by a Hong Kong notary public, then apply for an Apostille through the High Court of Hong Kong for Hague member states or for consular legalization through the destination state's consulate for non-member states; never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Beneficial Owner Passport and Domicile Evidence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing authority of the beneficial owner's residence or nationality; notarized in Hong Kong
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certify the photocopy as a true copy of the original by a Hong Kong notary public, then obtain an Apostille from the High Court of Hong Kong for Apostille Convention states or consular legalization from the destination state's consulate for non-member states; the two routes are mutually exclusive and sequential chaining is prohibited.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every beneficial owner, partner, general partner, director, shareholder, authorized signatory, and ultimate natural person behind the Foreign-Invested Partnership must be screened against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, UK HM Treasury consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Hong Kong Monetary Authority sanctions and notices, Hong Kong Customs and Excise strategic controls, and the PRC MOFCOM/MEAHOFCOM export-control and anti-money laundering lists. The screening must cover negative media, PEP status, source of wealth, and source of funds. Any hit triggers enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and a suspicious transaction report under Cap. 615.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies Registry e-Registry and Integrated Companies Information System (ICRIS) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: An English name is mandatory for the Foreign-Invested Partnership. A Chinese name may be added and must be in traditional characters; simplified Chinese characters are not acceptable for the statutory name. The Chinese name is not required to be a phonetic transliteration of the English name but must not be false or misleading. incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Not applicable as to Companies Act; the primary governing legislation is the Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38), particularly sections 3 (definition of partnership), 7 (continuation of partnership), 12 (rule that partnership property is held by partners) and 39 (joint and several liability), read together with the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) s.5, the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37) ss.4-9, and the Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) Part 2 for AML/CTF duties of a Foreign-Invested Partnership carrying on a designated non-financial business in Hong Kong.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department; and Limited Partnerships Section, Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Business Registration (Form IRBR1); Registration of Limited Partnership (Form LP1) and, if changes, Form LP2; annual Business Registration renewal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement for a Hong Kong Foreign-Invested Partnership. The partnership agreement may prescribe a subscribed capital schedule and drawdown mechanism; contributions become due only upon a call by the general partner. Where the entity is registered as a limited partnership, the amount contributed or agreed to be contributed by each limited partner must be stated in Form LP1, but no proof of deposit or escrow is required by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST PARTNERS’ MEETING OF [•] FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP (the “Partnership”), duly convened on [date] at [registered office], at which all partners were present or duly represented and waived notice. The following resolutions were proposed, seconded and unanimously passed as binding and enforceable decisions of the Partnership pursuant to the Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38) and the Partnership Deed. CAPITAL AND CAPITAL CONTRIBUTIONS. RESOLVED that the aggregate initial capital subscriptions of the Partners shall be as set out in the Partnership Deed, with a total committed capital of [US$[•]/HK$[•]] and no statutory paid-up minimum, and that each Partner shall remit their contribution to the Partnership’s designated bank account in accordance with the drawdown notice issued by the Managing Partner. RESOLVED FURTHER that additional capital may be called only by a further resolution of the General Partners, and any unremitted contribution shall carry interest at the rate specified in the Partnership Deed. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED that the Partnership shall establish and maintain multi-currency operating, payroll and SWIFT wire accounts with one or more banks licensed under the Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155). RESOLVED that the Managing Partner and the Chief Financial Officer of the Partnership be and are hereby appointed as authorized signatories, with a four-eyes rule requiring two authorized signatories for payments exceeding [US$5,000/HK$40,000], and that the appointed bank be furnished a certified copy of these resolutions together with an account-mandate form. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED that the address [•] located in Hong Kong is adopted as the registered office of the Partnership for service of process and statutory notices; that the office must remain open during ordinary business hours; and that any change of registered office must be filed with the Business Registration Office and, if applicable, the Limited Partnerships Section of the Companies Registry. STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED that [•] be appointed as Managing Partner; [•] as Partnership Secretary; [•] as the designated representative for business registration under Cap. 310; and [•] as the Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Officer under Cap. 615. Each officer is authorized to execute and file all forms and to instruct legal counsel to file with the Companies Registry, Inland Revenue Department, Marine Department and Labour Department. These resolutions are effective as of the date of this meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name search and partnership deed drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry Integrated Companies Registry Information System; private Hong Kong notary public / solicitor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the Integrated Companies Registry Information System to confirm the proposed English and Chinese name of the Foreign-Invested Partnership is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered body; instruct a Hong Kong solicitor to prepare the partnership deed and a notarial certificate of the deed for any PRC investor. The deed shall identify the partnership name, principal place of business, general and limited partners (if a limited partnership), profit-sharing ratios, capital commitment amounts, management authorities, and dissolution events. For any foreign corporate partner, attach certified certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and board resolutions authorizing partnership participation. Name reservation is not mandatory, but a search report should be preserved in the statutory records.
required_dossiers: personal identity documents/passports of all partners
certificates of incorporation and good standing of any corporate partner
board resolutions of corporate partners authorizing partnership membership
proof of Hong Kong registered address such as tenancy agreement or letter of support
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for being identical or confusingly similar, legal counsel will immediately submit a fresh ICRIS search with a reranked set of alternative names and refile within three business days. If the deed is rejected by the notary, correct attestation formalities and re-issue before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration application with Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IRBR1 to the Business Registration Office within one month after the partnership begins to carry on business in Hong Kong. Include the executed partnership deed, proof of identity for each partner, proof of the Hong Kong principal place of business, and landlord’s consent if the premises are leased. Pay the annual business registration fee and the business registration levy. The office will issue a Business Registration Certificate, which must be displayed at the principal place of business. If the Foreign-Invested Partnership has no physical office, a Hong Kong service address must be given. The certificate must be kept in the partnership's statutory records book together with the deed and the first partners’ resolutions.
required_dossiers: identity and address proof of all partners
tenancy agreement or proof of principal place of business
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, respond in writing to the Business Registration Office within twenty-one days with the missing document or explanation and pay any outstanding fee; for a suspension exceeding six months, submit a fresh Form IRBR1 together with a written justification and affidavit of continuous business intention.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Optional limited partnership registration with Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Limited Partnerships Section, Companies Registry, 14/F, Queensway Government Offices, 66 Queensway, Hong Kong
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If limited liability is required, file Form LP1 together with the executed limited partnership deed at the Companies Registry Limited Partnerships Section within seven days after formation. The form must state the partnership name, nature of business, principal place of business, full name and address of every general and limited partner, and the amount contributed or agreed to be contributed by each limited partner. Attach the declaration of the general partner confirming compliance with the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37) and pay the statutory registration fee. Upon issuance of the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership, the entity may use the words “Limited Partnership” and must file any changes in particulars on Form LP2. A limited partner who takes part in management will lose limited liability.
required_dossiers: identity and address of general and limited partners
declaration of compliance by general partner
proof of principal place of business in Hong Kong
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry raises an objection to the name or any required particular, amend Form LP1 and the corresponding deed clause and refile; if the Registrar refuses registration, apply for a review by the Registrar under the Companies Registry procedure and ultimately appeal to the District Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening, banking authorization and AML onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any bank licensed under the Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155) in Hong Kong; compliance with the Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Approach a licensed bank in Hong Kong to open the operating, payroll, and multi-currency SWIFT wire accounts. Present the Business Registration Certificate, Limited Partnership Certificate if registered, certified partnership deed, first partners’ resolution, and an account mandate executed by the authorized signatories. Complete all know-your-customer and beneficial ownership forms, including the identity and source of wealth of every partner. For multi-currency payroll operations, demonstrate the remittance schedule to seafarers and the AML compliance framework, including source-of-funds evidence for capital contributions. Maintain separate client and operating accounts to avoid co-mingling. The bank may require a bank reference letter for non-Hong Kong partners.
required_dossiers: first partners’ resolution and account mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, provide a reference letter from a licensed solicitor or accountant, historical bank statements, and a full corporate chart; if the account application is declined, re-apply with an alternate Hong Kong licensed bank and adjust the mandate to meet the bank’s KYO standards.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral statutory licensing for ship crew recruitment agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Employment Agencies Division, Labour Department, Hong Kong; Marine Department, Seafarer Manning and Crew Services Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before placing seafarers, obtain the statutory Employment Agency Licence under Part XII of the Employment Ordinance (Cap. 57). File the standard employment agency application with the Labour Department, specifying the dedicated office address, the responsible person, and the prohibition on charging fees to job seekers. For maritime operations, notify the Marine Department of the seafarer recruitment and placement service under the Merchant Shipping legislation, and submit evidence that written seafarer employment contracts comply with the Maritime Labour Convention 2006, that medical fitness certificates and STCW certificates are verified, and that no placement fees are charged to seafarers. The licence must be issued before the agency advertises any vacancy. If vessels sail under a foreign flag, obtain the flag-state manning licence or an equivalency certificate from the relevant consul.
required_dossiers: certified copy of Business Registration Certificate
certified copy of Limited Partnership Certificate (if any)
proposed agency office lease and landlord consent
identity and police/criminal record certificates of the responsible manager
declaration of no fees charged to job seekers
seafarer contract template and Maritime Labour Convention compliance schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Labour Department issues a notice of refusal, submit written representations within fourteen days and, if needed, appeal to the Administrative Appeals Board; for Marine Department objections, provide a corrective statement of seafarer wage assessment, re-submit the contract template, and undergo an interview with Marine Department examiners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, employer return and ongoing AML / annual compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR; Joint Financial Intelligence Unit for suspicious transaction reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Business Registration Certificate is issued, notify the Inland Revenue Department if the partnership employs staff by submitting Employer’s Registration Form (IR24) and any necessary Employer’s Return. The partnership itself is not subject to profits tax on a pass-through basis; each partner’s assessable share is reported separately. Appoint a designated representative for service of process and an Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Officer required under Cap. 615 for a designated non-financial business. Maintain accounting records sufficient to meet the Inland Revenue Ordinance s.51C requirement for at least seven years. File any suspicious transaction report with the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit. Renew the Business Registration Certificate annually before the anniversary date and file any changes in particulars with the Companies Registry.
required_dossiers: projection of profits and pass-through allocation statement
appointment letter of MLRO and designated representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Inland Revenue Department questions the pass-through allocation, file a detailed explanation and underlying partnership deed within twenty-one days and request an extension if needed; if a suspicious transaction report is queried, co-operate with the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit and engage legal counsel before the statutory deadline expires.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – ISIC 5222 is a maritime crewing and workforce coordination agency; there is no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operation under ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx. Sectoral employer licensing and maritime labour notification are addressed in SOP Step 5.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable for industrial or physical operating license. The entity is required to hold an Employment Agency Licence under Part XII of the Employment Ordinance (Cap. 57) and, if placing seafarers, to file a Marine Department vessel-manning notification; neither is an industrial permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category X under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499); no Schedule 2 designated project exists for an office-based crew recruitment agency, and no construction, manufacturing, smokestack or landfill activity is involved.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable – zero industrial wastewater, zero VOC emission ceiling, zero hazardous waste generation; office sewage must discharge to municipal sewers under the Water Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 358) and municipal solid waste must be collected under the Waste Disposal Ordinance (Cap. 354).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for industrial fire safety or dangerous-goods storage. The registered office must nevertheless comply with the Fire Safety (Commercial Premises) Ordinance (Cap. 502) and the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509), including adequate means of escape, emergency lighting, fire extinguishers, and a basic first-aid kit. No Civil Defense fire permit is required for an office-only tenant.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online electronic portal: Electronic Tax Service Platform (e-Tax) of the STA. For the Hong Kong SAR partner/investor, the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department (IRD) is the separate competent authority for Hong Kong profits tax, but the mainland-registered Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) itself has no Hong Kong tax registration and is registered with the PRC tax authorities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File the Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) with the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) under the Partnership Enterprise Law and the Foreign Investment Law; the AMR issues a Business License containing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory taxpayer identification number (TIN) and VAT identification number for the FIP. Step 2: Within 30 days after issuance of the Business License, complete tax registration through the STA e-Tax platform at the competent tax office, submitting the partnership agreement, partner register, foreign investor identification documents, legal representative identity, PRC bank account details, and the crew recruitment/crew management business scope. Step 3: The competent STA office enters the FIP into the VAT taxpayer database and records whether the FIP is a small-scale taxpayer or a general VAT taxpayer; general VAT taxpayer status is compulsory once annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000, or may be elected voluntarily if the FIP maintains proper accounting. Step 4: Apply for the all-digital electronic invoice (e-invoice) quota and link the USCC to the national e-invoice service platform; all subsequent VAT invoices, customs declarations, and foreign-exchange receipts will be automatically reconciled through the e-Tax data environment. Step 5: For each non-resident partner, the FIP must report the partner's home-jurisdiction tax reference number to the STA; if the non-resident partner has no PRC TIN, the tax authority will create an internal non-resident filing record for withholding on China-source partnership allocations. Step 6: A foreign non-resident entity supplying crew agency services into mainland China without forming a mainland FIP must separately register for VAT under its own name with the STA at the place of performance, using its foreign tax reference, the offshore service contract, and the non-resident's local contact details; the STA will assign a non-resident taxpayer record for VAT filing and invoice issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - the PRC-registered FIP is fiscally transparent for Enterprise Income Tax (EIT) purposes; the partnership itself is not an EIT taxpayer. Each partner, whether corporate or individual, resident or non-resident, is taxed on its distributable share of partnership income under the EIT Law or Individual Income Tax Law, as applicable. For VAT purposes, by contrast, the FIP is itself a taxable person and must account for output VAT, input VAT, and export zero-rating.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None in the US check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch sense. PRC tax law applies mandatory partnership transparency; no entity-level corporate income tax election exists for a partnership. The only available election is the voluntary registration as a general VAT taxpayer, which is an indirect-tax status election, not an income-tax election. The PRC-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement may be invoked by a qualifying HK partner to reduce withholding rates, but that is a treaty relief mechanism, not a domestic entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China (mainland China); Hong Kong SAR does not impose VAT, GST, or general sales tax and has no separate indirect tax registration for the mainland FIP.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable turnover is the statutory threshold requiring compulsory registration as a general VAT taxpayer. All newly formed FIPs must complete tax/VAT registration within 30 days of the Business License regardless of turnover. Small-scale taxpayers are those with annual taxable sales not exceeding RMB 5,000,000; non-resident suppliers with no mainland establishment must register from the first taxable supply performed in mainland China, with no de minimis turnover exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT invoices are cleared through the STA Golden Tax Phase IV environment. The FIP must issue all-digital electronic invoices (e-invoices) through the STA national e-invoice service platform or approved tax-control equipment, transmitting invoice data to the STA in near real-time via API/XML interfaces. Each invoice is authenticated by the STA and receives a unique tax-control code and anti-fraud QR/digital stamp before finalization; the STA automatically reconciles e-invoice data with VAT returns, customs declarations, and foreign-exchange receipts. Paper or manually completed invoices are not accepted for export zero-rating or input VAT credit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (i) physical goods exported from mainland China - such as ship stores, uniforms, and crew safety equipment sold to a non-resident shipowner - only when the goods are covered by a PRC Customs export declaration and the export proceeds are collected from the overseas buyer; and (ii) cross-border taxable services supplied to a non-resident recipient and consumed wholly outside mainland China. Maritime crew recruitment and crew management services supplied to a non-resident shipowner/operator for a vessel engaged in an international voyage can qualify for 0% VAT treatment where the service is consumed offshore and the consideration is paid in foreign currency by the non-resident principal. Services performed or consumed in mainland China, including recruitment of Chinese seafarers, domestic payroll processing, training in China, or crew agency margins sourced from China-resident payers, remain subject to VAT at 6%. The FIP must provide a complete audit file demonstrating the offshore nature of the service and the corresponding receipt of foreign exchange.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) for each physical export shipment
Bill of Lading or Master Air Waybill showing the overseas consignee/port of discharge
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign-currency receipt/collection advice evidencing foreign-exchange repatriation
Signed offshore service agreement or crew management contract naming the non-resident shipowner/operator and specifying the international voyage
Commercial invoice and e-invoice statement expressly recording the 0% VAT treatment
Port clearance or vessel itinerary/IMO documentation proving the vessel's call at a PRC port and subsequent international voyage
Crew lists and seafarer employment contracts demonstrating that the crew were supplied to the non-resident operator
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA Golden Tax IV system cross-matches export declarations, bills of lading, e-invoices, VAT returns, contracts, and foreign-exchange receipts. If export proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days, or the supporting documents cannot be produced, the 0% rate is revoked and output VAT is assessed at the applicable rate, with late-payment interest of 0.05% per day computed from the original filing date. Fraudulent, seriously incorrect, or unsupported zero-rating claims are treated as tax evasion under Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law of the People's Republic of China; the STA retrospectively claws back the entire VAT refund/zero-rated input credit, imposes an administrative penalty of 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax, and may refer the case for criminal prosecution under the Criminal Law for export-tax-refund or VAT-invoice fraud. Recovery periods may extend to 20 years for concealed fraudulent claims, and the FIP can lose general VAT taxpayer status and future eligibility for zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Hong Kong operates as a Special Administrative Region with complete foreign exchange freedom. There is no central bank in the traditional sense; the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) implements the Linked Exchange Rate System through a currency board, maintaining a USD/HKD band of 7.75–7.85. Both current account transactions and capital account transactions are freely convertible for residents and non-residents alike. The HKD is issued by three note-issuing banks under 100% backing in the Currency Board Account. No surrender requirements, exchange controls, prior approval mechanisms, or profit repatriation restrictions exist. Non-resident investors may freely remit dividends, royalties, and capital gains abroad. Cross-border flows between mainland China and Hong Kong remain subject to the People's Bank of China and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) in the mainland, but once funds reach Hong Kong they face no convertibility or remittance hurdles. The currency is fully convertible and there is no administrative distinction between current and capital account treatments in foreign currency pricing. Profit remittance hurdles are absent, and there is no statutory requirement to convert any export earnings into HKD or any other domestic currency. This makes Hong Kong a neutral liquidity hub and a treasury gateway for a Foreign-Invested Partnership engaged in ship crew recruitment, facilitating multi-currency payroll clearing through global correspondent banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. The Hong Kong SAR imposes no export proceeds surrender rules. All export foreign exchange proceeds may be retained in HKD, USD, or any other freely convertible currency. There are no statutory timelines for conversion and no mandatory ratios.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (HSBC)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account with RMB Clearing via CHATS

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI services providers operating without an HKMA-authorized banking license are not legally permitted to maintain deposit-taking or remittance accounts for Hong Kong corporate entities under the Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155). A Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) must therefore rely on domestic licensed banks. Licensed virtual banks (e.g., ZA Bank Limited, Airstar Bank Limited) are viable for low-risk operations but may present limitations in multi-currency payroll clearing and compliance acceptance for partnership structures. The optimal viability rating for the target crewing agency is Low to Medium for fintech/EMI-only solutions and High for the Tier-1 banks listed above, because these banks possess global correspondent clearing lines necessary for seafarer payroll disbursements and cross-border trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Hong Kong FIP, the Inland Revenue Ordinance requires no physical director residence in Hong Kong, but HKMA's AML/CTF guidelines require financial institutions to verify the identity and beneficial ownership of corporate customers. In practice, HSBC, Standard Chartered, and Bank of China (Hong Kong) permit remote account opening via video conferencing for low-risk customers with an in-branch interview for final KYC sign-off. A consular proxy opening is not generally accepted for an FIP; each general and limited partner must personally complete identification procedures, either in-branch or through a recognised private-banking remote process. A physical presence in Hong Kong is not statutorily mandated, but the bank may require the local company secretary or a designated partner to attend a verification meeting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Partners' beneficial ownership obscured by multi-layer limited partnership interests or nominee holdings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original FIP registration certificate from Hong Kong Companies Registry, full Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA), a signed Beneficial Ownership Declaration and covering letter, certified copies of passports and proof of residential address for every general and limited partner, a chart of the ownership cascade, and audited financial statements or source-of-wealth documents for each partner holding 25% or more capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crew recruitment exposure to maritime sanctions, ship blacklists, or illegal fishing/OFAC SDN involvement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Employment Agency Licence (Maritime) issued under the Labour Department of the Hong Kong Government, Maritime Labour Certificate under the Maritime Labour Convention 2006, sample crew employment contracts with standardized remuneration, a list of vessel owners and hiring entities, and evidence that all vessels are screened against OFAC, EU, UN, and HKMA-published sanctions lists, plus an independent third-party sanctions screening report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a mainland Chinese parent to the FIP could trigger anti-money-laundering red flags if no proof of outward investment approval.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PRC SAFE ODI/FDI registration certificate for the mainland parent's investment in the Hong Kong FIP, bank debit advices showing the remittance purpose as Direct Investment with the appropriate SAFE trade item code, a Hong Kong CPA's capital contribution assurance report, and an accountant's declaration confirming the injected amount matches partnership agreements and is not derived from undisclosed third-party sources.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume disbursements to multiple seafarer beneficiaries in several countries with varied employment terms, which may appear as a potential worker-exploitation or money-mule scheme.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete crew payroll register, individual employment contracts and seafarer passports, Certificates of Competency, insurance policies covering P&I and employer's liability, a list of beneficiary bank branches, and a written protocol that every new crew member receives a direct payroll account in their own name, with monthly payroll reconciliation signed by the compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection from a mainland Chinese parent into the Hong Kong FIP requires, in the mainland leg, SAFE registration under the Outbound Direct Investment (ODI) regime, and bank instructions using a Cross-Border RMB Settlement Purpose Code (e.g., 'Direct Investment' from SAFE's trade item code table) or an equivalent USD remittance code. The Hong Kong receiving bank will credit the funds to the FIP's Capital Escrow Account with supporting remittance details stating 'Capital Contribution – FIP Name'. An independent Hong Kong CPA should issue a Capital Contribution Verification Report (non-statutory assurance) within 30 days to evidence that the injection is fully paid and is not a disguised loan. A SWIFT MT103 with full field 72 advice is the preferred premium rail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For vessel crew salaries, use SWIFT MT103 individual credits or MT102 batch payment instructions to beneficiaries in their domestic currency. For ship chandler and port supplies, Commercial Letters of Credit through the issuing bank's SWIFT MT700/MT754 structure are accepted, while Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) follow SWIFT MT400/MT410 series instructions via the collecting bank. All outbound payments must align with the invoicing through the crewing agency's operational account and be supported by employment contracts, port service invoices, and vessel disbursement instructions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards with tenors up to 12 months in HKD/USD/CNH/EUR/GBP
Cross-currency interest rate swaps between HKD, USD, and CNH
Vanilla FX call and put options for seafarer payroll future obligations
Offshore CNH NDFs which are permissible but normally replaced by deliverable CNH swaps in Hong Kong due to the fully convertible CNH market

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of a Hong Kong Limited Partnership / Limited Partnership Fund (prescribed form LPF3 or LP3, as applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: LPF: within 42 days after each anniversary of registration; legacy limited partnership: within 21 days after each anniversary of registration; amended statement of particulars also due within 15 to 30 days of any change in partners or registered particulars.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fees escalate under the applicable Ordinance; continued default exposes the partnership to prosecution, a fine at criminal level, daily default fines, and administrative deregistration by the Companies Registry, which also removes the limited liability shield for general partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month before expiration of the current one-year or three-year business registration certificate, as demanded by the renewal notice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew without reasonable excuse is an offence; late renewal attracts penalty fees, risk of prosecution, a fine of up to HK$5,000, and a daily default fine of HK$200, and the partnership cannot lawfully continue trading while unregistered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (BIR56A) and supporting payroll schedules for crew and shore staff
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April immediately following the Hong Kong fiscal year of assessment ending 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate estimated assessments, monetary penalties up to 300% of the tax undercharged, fines up to HK$10,000 per charge, and potential prosecution under the Inland Revenue Ordinance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return for partnerships (Form BIR51/BIR52) together with financial statements, tax computation, and auditor/certified accountant report when required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the period stated in the IRD notice, normally 1 month from issue date; where the partnership ceases business, within the prescribed period after cessation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessments may be raised under the Inland Revenue Ordinance; fines up to 300% of undercharged tax may be imposed for fraudulent or negligent filings, and the partnership may lose entitlement to claim deductions for that tax year.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employment Agency Licence renewal for the maritime crew recruitment and placement agency activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of the current licence or as stated on the licence; renewal application must be submitted at least 30 days before expiry for crew recruitment operations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a valid employment agency licence is a criminal offence with fines up to HK$350,000 and imprisonment; the Labour Department may suspend or refuse renewal and issue cease-placement orders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registered office, corporate secretarial records, and statutory registers availability for inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Hong Kong Companies Registry and authorised law-enforcement/IRD inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous annual obligation; records must be kept at the Hong Kong registered office throughout the year and any change of registered office or registered particulars must be filed within 15 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-maintenance of registers may lead to administrative strike-off, fines at level 4 (HK$25,000), and a daily default fine of HK$700 while the default continues.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a Hong Kong private company or corporate wrapper, a statutory audit is mandatory unless the entity qualifies as a small private company or small private group under Cap. 622 s.746, i.e., annual turnover not exceeding HK$20,000,000, total assets not exceeding HK$10,000,000, and 50 or fewer employees. A Hong Kong partnership is not automatically audit-exempt: the Inland Revenue Department may require audited/certified financial statements whenever active trading creates taxable profits, and a statutory audit is mandatory for any Limited Partnership Fund whose constituent terms or regulatory status require one, as well as for any crewing agency licence holder subject to VET/MPF compliance or consolidated foreign parent reporting. Exceeding any one quantitative threshold triggers a full independent CPA audit under HKFRS.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), converged with IFRS; HKFRS for Private Entities is permitted for eligible smaller enterprises; IFRS applies whenever the entity is part of a foreign parent consolidation or statutory audit under HKFRS is required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foreign-Invested Partnership must maintain a Significant Controllers Register / Register of Partners at the Hong Kong registered office; all changes in individuals or legal entities with significant control, including share or partnership interest transfers, must be recorded within 7 days and confirmed in the next annual return. Any allotment or transfer affecting 5% or more of the ownership interest must be reported on the prescribed Companies Registry return within the 30-day reporting window. The Companies Registry may inspect the register on demand from IRD, police, and anti-money-laundering authorities; failure to maintain and confirm the register is a criminal offence carrying a level 4 fine and daily default penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Register of Partners (General and Limited Partners)
Register of Directors and Secretaries (where a corporate general partner is appointed)
Minute Book of partner meetings and partner resolutions
Register of Partnership Interest Transfers and Allotments

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per annum for a licensed Hong Kong registered agent, corporate secretarial filing and registered office address service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 12,000 per annum for a certified CPA audit, depending on crew payroll volume, transaction complexity, and IFRS consolidation requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 16.5% for corporations / 15% for unincorporated partnerships; two-tiered profits tax rate applies to the first HK$2 million of assessable profits at 8.25% for corporations and 7.5% for unincorporated businesses
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays, free-zone exemptions or patent box regime. Hong Kong applies a territorial source profits tax, meaning offshore-sourced income may be exempt from tax. The two-tiered profits tax rate lowers the effective rate on the first HK$2 million of assessable profits. Qualifying research and development expenditure benefits from enhanced deduction of up to 300%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profits Tax Return for Partnerships (Inland Revenue Department Form BIR52), filed through the IRD eTAX electronic filing portal; corporations would use BIR51, but a Foreign-Invested Partnership files BIR52
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be completed and filed within one month from the date of issue of BIR52. For a 31 December fiscal year-end, the return is ordinarily issued in April and due by early May; for a 30 June fiscal year-end, the return is ordinarily issued in November and due by mid-December. A tax representative may apply to the IRD for an extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal business name, Chinese/English name, business registration number, principal place of business in Hong Kong, and correspondence address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The FIP must state the precise legal entity form and the Hong Kong business registration certificate number. Non-resident partners should ensure a valid Hong Kong address for service of documents is provided, and must not use a registered agent maildrop where the IRD requires actual substance. Failure to provide an accurate address can result in assessment being sent to the last known address and default judgment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity/nature of trade, including the ISIC/NAICS classification and description of crew recruitment and maritime staffing services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the actual activity as an ISIC 5222 ship crew recruitment agency, including vessel crew placement, payroll management and seafarer logistics. The FIP must separately identify services physically performed in Hong Kong versus services performed abroad, because the Hong Kong tax is territorial and only profits sourced in Hong Kong are chargeable. A bare assertion that crew management is offshore will be scrutinized against the IRD's DIPN 24 offshore claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover/receipts for the year, including commissions, management fees, crew payroll gross-ups and reimbursements, and any foreign source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all gross income accrued or received in Hong Kong. For crew recruitment, commissions from ship owners located abroad do not automatically become Hong Kong-sourced income if the negotiation, contracting and profit-generating activities are performed outside Hong Kong. To claim non-assessable offshore income, the FIP must file an offshore claim and provide full supporting evidence of where the core income-generating activities were physically performed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses and additions to assessable profits: crew wages, insurance, listing fees, international communication, travel, legal and professional expenses, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses are deductible only under IRO section 16 when incurred in producing assessable profits. Expenses attributable to offshore income should not be claimed against Hong Kong profits. Add back non-deductible items such as capital expenditure, personal withdrawals, attendance fees to partners, and penalties. The FIP must prepare a reconciliation from accounting profits to assessable profits and maintain contemporaneous evidence for all cross-border crew payroll payments to related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted net assessable profit or adjusted loss after applying all statutory additions and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a partnership, the adjusted profit is computed at partnership level but tax is assessed on each partner separately. Non-resident partners are only taxable on their share of Hong Kong-sourced profits. If the FIP is seeking treaty relief, the adjusted profit must be allocated in accordance with each partner's profit-sharing ratio, and the non-resident partner's Hong Kong situs income must be separately declared.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner allocation schedule: name, tax residence, share of capital, profit sharing ratio, and allocated assessable profit for each resident and non-resident partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List every foreign partner's full name, address, tax identification number and country of tax residence. For a Mainland China partner, attach a Tax Residency Certificate and relevant China-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement claim to avoid double taxation. For corporate partners, confirm the beneficial ownership threshold for treaty relief and provide supporting documentation. The FIP must also affirm whether any related party transaction exceeds the transfer pricing documentation thresholds set out under DIPN 58.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file BIR52 without reasonable excuse is punishable under IRO section 80(1) by a fine of up to HK$10,000 and a further daily fine. If tax is undercharged as a result of omission or incorrect returns, the IRD may impose additional tax of up to three times the amount undercharged. Fraudulent evasion under IRO section 82A carries a maximum fine of HK$50,000, additional tax up to three times the tax undercharged, and imprisonment for up to three years. Failure to notify chargeability to tax can also result in penalties under IRO section 51 and 80.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Hong Kong does not impose any statutory dividend withholding tax. Distributions or profit shares remitted by the Foreign-Invested Partnership to partners, whether resident or non-resident, are not subject to a separate dividend withholding tax under the Inland Revenue Ordinance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief under the China-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement or other comprehensive DTA, the non-resident partner must first obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) / Certificate of Residence from the tax authority of the partner's jurisdiction of residence. The partner must substantiate beneficial ownership of the profit share and demonstrate that it is not a conduit or shell recipient. The FIP must retain the TRC, a properly completed treaty claim form, and evidence that the partner has real economic substance, including the ability to manage, benefit from and assume risk of the income. In the absence of substantiation, the IRD will deny treaty benefits and impose the statutory rates and penalties.

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty withholding in Hong Kong: royalty paid to a non-resident corporation for use of intellectual property in Hong Kong is subject to deemed profits of 30% of gross royalties and the payer must withhold 30% x 16.5% = 4.95%, while a royalty to a non-resident individual is subject to 30% x 15% = 4.5%. Interest has no general statutory withholding tax, but interest income arising from a Hong Kong trade, profession or business remains taxable on a territorial basis. Under the China-Hong Kong DTA, interest may be taxable at 7% in the source state and royalties at 5%, provided the beneficial owner is a resident of the other side; dividends may be taxed at 5% if the beneficial owner is a company holding at least 25% equity, otherwise 10% in certain source-state scenarios, but Hong Kong in its present law does not levy outbound dividend withholding.
